gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a named reviewer measured the Fluance RT81's speed: Thom Moon at SoundStage! Access (15 Feb 2024) used a phone speed app and read 33.5 rpm at 33⅓, about 0.5% fast, and 45.16 rpm at 45, with wow of ±0.17% and ±0.21%. That is within Fluance's current published ±1.00% speed tolerance but outside the ±0.1% Moon quoted from Fluance at the time.
standout_why: I compared against three result pages. valveandvinyl.com/turntables/crosley-alternatives (dated 2026-11-07) says its picks are 'spec-and-price analyses, not listening tests'. Every figure on it is a maker claim: AT-LP70X <0.25% W&F, RT81 0.2% W&F and ≥67 dB A-weighted S/N, AT-LP120XUSB <0.2% W&F. It has no measured speed, wow or noise for any candidate. The fewbetter.com fetch returned an unrelated catalogue page with no turntable figures. vinylpickup.com would not load (TLS certificate error), so I did not check it. TechRadar's fetch came back truncated with no figures. I did not open platterandplinth, stylusandsound, insideouthomereviews, thebrickfantastic, worldisround, itechguides, techyorker, sekin or burtonacoustix, so rival coverage here is partly unchecked. Of the pages I could read, none gives a measurement credited to a named person.
decides: This confirms the RT81 for a shopper who wants manual control, and it does not overturn the pick. In a named reviewer's test its speed ran about 0.5% fast, within Fluance's published ±1%, and wow was ±0.17–0.21%, close to the 0.2% claim. Moon said it 'didn't seem to affect the music'. The finding is one phone-app test of one product, not a lab bench. No candidate has a comparable named measurement, so it cannot rank the RT81 against the AT-LP70X or the Sony. It can only show that the RT81 roughly meets its own specs.

findings.label: Measured platter speed at 33⅓ rpm
findings.source_title: SoundStage! Access: Fluance RT81 Turntable and Audio-Technica AT-VM95E Cartridge (Thom Moon)
findings.note: The page says 'Created: 15 February 2024'. Moon measured with the RPM app on his phone. He wrote 'about 0.55% fast', but 33.5/33.333 = 1.0050, so +0.50%. The review title pairs the RT81 with an AT-VM95E, while Fluance's RT81 page today lists the AT95E as the bundled cartridge. Platter speed does not depend on the cartridge.

findings.label: Measured wow at 33⅓ rpm
findings.source_title: SoundStage! Access: Fluance RT81 Turntable and Audio-Technica AT-VM95E Cartridge (Thom Moon)
findings.note: Phone RPM app; the article calls the figure 'estimated'. Flutter was not measured separately.

findings.label: Measured platter speed and wow at 45 rpm
findings.source_title: SoundStage! Access: Fluance RT81 Turntable and Audio-Technica AT-VM95E Cartridge (Thom Moon)
findings.note: 45.16/45 = 1.0036. Moon: 'Both speed measurements are higher than Fluance's claims, but this didn't seem to affect the music during my listening.' The claim he compared against was ±0.1% speed variation.

findings.label: Maker's current published speed variation and wow & flutter, for comparison
findings.value: ±1.00% speed variation; 0.2% wow & flutter; S/N ≥67 dB A-weighted / ≥60 dB unweighted (20 kHz LPF); $299.99
findings.source_title: Fluance RT81 Hi-Fi Vinyl Turntable Record Player with Diamond Needle
findings.note: Maker claim, not a measurement. Fluance now publishes ±1.00%, not the ±0.1% Moon quoted in 2024, so his +0.50% reading is inside today's spec. The page lists the bundled cartridge as the AT95E, phono output 3.5 mV, and the preamp as PHONO/LINE switchable. It gives no preamp gain figure.

findings.label: Measured low-frequency motor noise relative to signal
findings.value: 25 dB below a 1 kHz test tone recorded at −14 dB
findings.source_title: Secrets of Home Theater and High Fidelity: Fluance RT81 Turntable, Cartridge, Phono Preamplifier Review (John E. Johnson, Jr.)
findings.note: Review dated 15 June 2016, an earlier production run at an MSRP of $249.99. Johnson played a 1 kHz test LP and analysed it with SpectraPLUS and a Lynx L22 sound card. He did not measure wow and flutter: 'I don't have a way of measuring it in bench testing.'

findings.label: Measured channel crosstalk
findings.value: 20 dB below the test signal at 1 kHz
findings.source_title: Secrets of Home Theater and High Fidelity: Fluance RT81 Turntable, Cartridge, Phono Preamplifier Review (John E. Johnson, Jr.)
findings.note: 1 kHz tone recorded at 0 dB in the left channel only. Johnson: 'right on the factory specification'. He also checked that the counterweight's 2 g setting reads 2 g on a Clearaudio gauge. 2016 review; he wished the built-in preamp had 'higher output (0.5 volts)'.

unsourced: Measured speed, wow/flutter or noise for the Audio-Technica AT-LP70X or AT-LP70XBT. Searches found only the maker spec (<0.25% WTD, >55 dB) and listening-only reviews from What Hi-Fi?, Digital Trends and CNET. I found no review that measured either model.

Measured figures for the Fluance RT81+. I found no review of the RT81+ that measured it. Search summaries that labelled Moon's SoundStage numbers as RT81+ results were wrong: that review is of the RT81.

Measured figures for the Sony PS-LX3BT and PS-LX310BT. What Hi-Fi?, TechRadar and hifi.de reviews turned up no measurements in search. The only Hi-Fi News Sony lab report found is for the PS-FL7, a different model.

A lab measurement of the Audio-Technica AT-LP120XUSB. An Australian Hi-Fi / Newport Test Labs report probably exists (Steve Holding, July 2020), but Everand returned 404 and PressReader returned 403, so I could not read its figures. Frieve's review says 'No independent third-party measurements are available'. I found no Hi-Fi News, Archimago or ASR test of this model.
Michael Fremer's AnalogPlanet review of the Fluance RT81, which may contain speed measurements. The page returned HTTP 403.
Comparisons from vinylpickup.com ('19 Tested'), which would not load because of a TLS certificate error, so I could not check whether it publishes its own measurements.
